sections.title: Linear combinations
beats: A linear combination means scale some vectors, then add them.
With î = [1,0] and ĵ = [0,1], any point is a·î + b·ĵ.
The span is every point you can reach that way.
sections.example: Two ingredients in different amounts make a whole range of drinks.
sections.sayback: Define span in your own words.

sections.title: Basis
beats: A basis is a minimum set of vectors whose span covers the space.
If one vector is just a stretch of another, it adds nothing new. That's linear dependence.
Two independent arrows span a plane. Three can span 3D space.
sections.example: BTC and 'BTC ×2 leverage' are dependent. They point the same way.
sections.sayback: Why does a dependent vector add nothing?
sections.tieback: Quant link: highly correlated assets ≈ dependent vectors, so they give little diversification.
